reference: arXiv:1510.07412 (Halbwachs et al., Paper II). Native DOI/source projection only.
scope: All three specified systems, 10+6+7 recovered processed PIONIER epochs. First full 2D position per system is the only measured sky input. Remaining 9/5/6 form the measured held set. The search-exposed epoch 56937.179 at 2.28 mas is the earliest HIP117186 anchor. Four later positions used an imposed H-band flux ratio learned from the observations. Reuse and calibration preclude an independent raw interferogram or chronological real-time forecast.
source_rights: Use Table orbSB2 RV-only elements (old and new spectroscopy; HIP14157 HERMES, both others SOPHIE) and tab:HIP2 original single-star varpi_SS only. Exclude tab:Masse, adjusted Hipparcos AO, full visual elements, every target separation/angle, all flux ratios and target-scaled error ellipses. Sample clocks nominal MJD+0.5 versus BJD-2400000; source table does not identify the full barycentric time correction for each interferometric exposure. Offline catalogue transfer uses spectra from after some sky observations.
equations: Angular a sin i from the sum of independently published minimum barycentric semimajor axes (Gm), AU=149.5978707 Gm, historical annual parallax in mas. Confirm from K1+K2, observed P and published Ptrue correction v0/c. X=cos E−e,Y=sqrt(1−e²)sin E; (u,v)=R(omega1)(X,Y). Using secondary periastron instead rotates all coordinates by pi and cancels. sky p=a RΩ(u, ±c v), c=|cos i|. Earliest measured rho0,PA0 permits radial and signed along-anchor projection; absolute perpendicular sign is globally unidentifiable without another directional input.
arms: Register marginal as sole primary: isotropic orientation (uniform c) with log-uniform angular semimajor-axis prior, conditioning on exact processed anchor norm gives uniform c before an independent approximate Gaussian error likelihood for observed A. Scale s_A=hypot(parallax_SE*(a1+a2)/AU,parallax*(a1_SE+a2_SE)/AU). RV covariance unavailable; summing component errors is a declared sensitivity assumption. Marginal predicts expectations of radius and signed projection separately. Source-aligned constrained least-squares inversion is physical_fit; it is equivalent to the exact one-anchor algebra for a feasible nominal parallax. Infeasible nominal anchor explicitly projects to edge-on, reports raw c², preserves every row. Strong controls same records: physical_fit, face_on, edge_on, isotropic (no external distance likelihood), stationary. Two ±1-scale fits are diagnostics. No nonlinear/full data author joint fit can be used as a forecast; nominal constrained fit is its limited same-information geometric counterpart.
evaluation: Errors in mas in radius, and in rho_t cos(PA_t−PA_anchor). For each endpoint and arm compute each system's RMS across every held epoch, equal mean and maximum across three systems (four primary comparisons). Marginal must strictly beat the best of the five named controls on every aggregate. Preserve signed per-row residuals, all arms, global mirror branches for all vectors, one fixed handedness per system for diagnostic full vector RMS (never one sign per row), raw worst including whole trajectory. Fraction of observations in distance-free radius interval diagnostic only, not a sampled confidence interval.
preopening: Require all23 epochs and3 first anchor identities. Archive source tar and all forecasts locked before held response decoding. 4096-point midpoint integration post/flat prior; all predictions within .002 mas of 2048. Independent bisection of the monotone 1D geometric fit or edge solution must agree to 2e-7 mas on every registered coordinate. Numerical and source failures close the existing gate. No dropping epochs.
sensitivity: Before opening, archive primary marginal+direct predictions re-evaluated for every sign combination of four RV marginals P,T0,e,omega ±1 printed SE and a common ±.008d timestamp offset. Discrete diagnostic, no joint-covariance or continuum uncertainty claim. Preserve source's small-separation/fixed-flux flags and all worst systems. No calibrating on target error ellipses or held angles.
